label: copy phase: just-copied token was i (input i), from recall position 2 on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in original or delimiter steps), when the fed-back input is the letter i, i.e. the model has just output i and is now recalling the next original token. Input i carries 94% of the activation mass; input u gives weak activations (~5.5% of mass), v and m almost nothing. Nearly silent at recall_idx 0-1 (rate rises from recall_idx 2 and plateaus at 3+). It never fires on the first occurrence of a token in the sequence (in_first=0 throughout). Strongest activations in the top examples are on an i that will be followed by output u (i u bigram in the original); the last copy step (to_go 0) is included. Precision is limited: about 28% of copy-phase i inputs at recall_idx>=2 do not fire, and I did not find a simple condition that separates them. Adding to_go<=5 helped only slightly (dev F1 0.80 vs 0.79).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: i, u, v, -, m, <DEL>; least: 3, c, p, l) and the token being output (most: u, i, v, n, m, w; least: 3, l, -, z); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, recall_idx=5.
